notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json.

evals.query: report how many developers actively use the tool
expected_behavior: defines the event, filter, aggregation and window before producing a number
attaches a validation example - a concrete input set and the exact expected result
files the undecided part as Q<n> rather than picking a definition silently
evals.baseline: answers with a plausible-sounding definition of 'active' and moves straight to a query

evals.query: split the usage report by paid and trial seats
expected_behavior: greps for the emitter proving the seat field exists before using it
files Q<n> naming the missing field when no emitter writes it
declines to substitute a nearest-available proxy under the same metric name
evals.baseline: assumes the field exists and defines the split on it

evals.query: also add median command latency to the dashboard
expected_behavior: checks whether any R<n> asks for latency
cuts the metric and raises a finding targeting analysis when none does
evals.baseline: adds the metric because it seems useful

evals.query: the daily active count looks too low, fix the aggregation
expected_behavior: checks whether an existing M<n> already defines the behaviour
resolves as an implementation defect rather than adding a duplicate definition
evals.baseline: writes a second, subtly different definition of the same metric
